study.title: Ephesians 2 of spiritual death to the abode of God
study.overview: Ephesians 2 describes two great realities: first, the human condition without Christ - spiritual death, slavery to sin and exclusion from the life of the covenant; then, the sovereign intervention of God in Christ, which saves by grace, unites Jews and Gentiles in one people and makes the church an indwelling of God by the Spirit. The chapter not only explains how someone is saved, but also for which he is saved: to live in good works, in reconciliation and in holy communion.

outline.title: The old condition: dead, dominated and guilty
outline.explanation: Paul recalls that the Ephesians lived in offenses and sins, following the course of this world and the influence of the spiritual power of evil. This life was marked by desires of the flesh and the condition of wrath, showing that the problem of the human being is not only external behavior, but a spiritual situation of death before God.

outline.title: The Great Turn: God Saves by Grace for Good Works
outline.explanation: Against the picture of human misery, Paul highlights the mercy and love of God. Salvation happens to Christ: God gives life, rises and spiritually enthrones believers. It is received by grace through faith, without human merit, and has a clear ethical purpose: the saved are recreated in Christ to walk in the good works that God has prepared.

outline.title: Far and near: Christ overthrows separation
outline.explanation: Paul sends the Gentiles to remember their old condition: without Christ, outside the community of Israel, without hope and without God. But now, by the blood of Christ, those who were far ahead are approached. Christ is our peace: he creates a new people, puts an end to enmity and grants both access to the Father by one Spirit.

outline.title: A new citizenship and a new temple
outline.explanation: Believers are no longer foreigners, but members of God's family. The church is described as a seated building on apostles and prophets, having Christ as the main stone, growing to be a holy temple. The culmination is that God dwells there by the Spirit, making the people united in Christ their living abode.

study.context: The chapter addresses the believers of Ephesus and counters what they were and what they were and what they are in Christ. The notes highlight that Paul wants to lead them to remember their old misery to produce humility, gratitude and love. There is also a contrast between Jews and Gentiles, both attained by the same work of Christ and gathered in one body.
study.theology: Chapter theology emphasizes human depravity and divine initiative in salvation. The human being appears as spiritually dead, unable to save himself by merit or works. The grace of God is the cause of salvation, and faith is the means of receiving it, not the basis of pride. In Christ, God also creates a new humanity, removing the enmity between peoples and forming a church that is a holy temple and abode of God. Thus, salvation is personal and communal: it reconciles the sinner with God and the believers among themselves. Good works are not the root of salvation, but its fruit prepared by God.

scholarViews.insight: Paul's readers were spiritually dead because of disobedience and sins, under the influence of the devil's power and condemned with the rest of the world.
Salvation does not come from ourselves or from human works; this excludes any pride, because glory must be given to the Lord.
Christ reconciled Jews and Gentiles so that, as one spiritual body, they would leave their contentions and live according to the gospel.

questions: What changes in the way of seeing oneself when one understands that salvation is the gift of God and not human conquest?
In what practical ways does the church today still need to live as one people, and not as groups separated by preferences or origin?
If God has prepared good works for the saved, what concrete signs show that we are walking in them?
study.practice: Read this chapter as a call to memory, humility and unity. Remember who you were without Christ to thank you more deeply for grace. Examine whether your faith is producing works consistent with the gospel. And actively seek reconciliation with other believers, avoiding any attitude that reinforces separations that Christ has already overthrown. The local church should be lived as a family, not as a disputed field.
study.uncertainty: The notes provided are incomplete in some verses and do not allow to reconstruct all the details of each comment. Some interpretive formulations about the "law of commandments in ordinances" and the "mointing" vary between the commentators; here they were presented as possible readings, not as an absolute definition of the text. There is also no basis on the notes to accurately identify external historical references beyond what the chapter itself and the comments mention.
